name: Amass
description: Domain attack-surface mapping and DNS enumeration.
example2: amass enum -d example.com -o amass.txt
safety: Use passive mode for low-impact discovery. Active enumeration requires scope approval.

name: Subfinder
description: Discovers subdomains from passive online sources.
example2: subfinder -d example.com -o subdomains.txt
safety: Configure provider API keys where needed; validate results before reporting.

name: theHarvester
description: Collects publicly indexed emails, hosts, and related domain intelligence.
installation: git clone https://github.com/laramies/theHarvester.git && cd theHarvester && pipx install .
example2: theHarvester -d example.com -b duckduckgo -l 100
safety: Search provider availability and syntax can change between releases.

name: Recon-ng
description: Modular framework for organising web reconnaissance workflows.
example2: marketplace search domains
safety: Some modules require API keys; install only trusted modules.

name: SpiderFoot
description: Automates OSINT collection across domains, IPs, emails, and usernames.
installation: git clone https://github.com/smicallef/spiderfoot.git && cd spiderfoot && python3 -m venv venv && . venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt
example2: python3 sf.py -h
safety: Run locally and select modules carefully; scans can generate third-party requests.

name: Shodan
description: Search engine for internet-connected systems and service banners.
installation: python3 -m pip install --user shodan && shodan init YOUR_API_KEY
example2: shodan host 8.8.8.8
safety: API access and query limits depend on account plan.

name: Censys
description: Searches internet-facing hosts, certificates, and exposed services.
installation: Web service; create an account at https://search.censys.io/
example1: Search the Hosts interface for example.com
example2: Search Certificates for names matching example.com
safety: Use account/API credentials securely and respect plan limits.

name: ZoomEye
description: Internet cyberspace search engine for hosts and exposed services.
example2: Search: ip:8.8.8.8
safety: Validate asset ownership before any follow-up testing.

name: Nmap
description: Discovers hosts, ports, and service versions on authorised networks.
installation: sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y nmap
safety: Use only on networks and systems within your authorised scope.

name: Masscan
description: High-speed port scanner for explicitly authorised network ranges.
safety: Very high impact if misconfigured; keep rates low and scope narrow.

name: DNSRecon
description: Performs DNS record enumeration and zone-related checks.
example2: dnsrecon -d example.com -t soa
safety: Avoid intrusive tests unless explicitly authorised.

name: WHOIS
description: Queries public domain and IP registration records where available.
example2: whois 8.8.8.8
safety: Privacy protection and registry policies may hide registration details.

name: crt.sh
description: Searches certificate-transparency logs for certificates and related hostnames.
installation: No installation; use the web interface or curl.
example2: Open https://crt.sh/?q=example.com
safety: Certificate entries indicate issuance, not that a host is currently live.

name: SecurityTrails
description: Provides DNS history, subdomain, and domain intelligence.
installation: Web service; API access requires an account.
example1: Search example.com in the Domain Search interface
example2: Use the DNS History view for example.com
safety: Historical data can be incomplete; check current DNS independently.

name: Sherlock
description: Checks username presence across supported social networks and websites.
example2: sherlock user123 --print-found
safety: A matching username is not proof that accounts belong to the same person.

name: Maigret
description: Searches many sites for public profiles associated with a username.
example2: maigret user123 --html
safety: Confirm profile ownership using independent evidence; false positives occur.

name: WhatsMyName
description: Community-maintained username enumeration data and workflow.
example1: Open the project's JSON data and search for a site
example2: Use the project website list to manually verify a username
safety: Treat results as leads, not identity attribution.

name: GHunt
description: Investigates publicly exposed Google-related information using supported workflows.
example2: ghunt email
safety: Some functions require authentication; use only accounts/identifiers you are permitted to investigate.

name: WhatsMyName Web
description: Web interface for checking username presence on supported websites.
example1: Enter a test username in the search field
example2: Filter and manually open candidate profile links
safety: Do not infer identity from a username match alone.

name: Maltego
description: Visual link-analysis platform connecting people, domains, infrastructure, and organisations.
installation: Download the desktop installer from https://www.maltego.com/downloads/
example1: Create a Domain entity for example.com
example2: Run an available DNS Name transform on the domain
safety: Transforms and data access may require accounts or paid plans.

name: SpiderFoot HX
description: Hosted and enterprise-oriented OSINT investigation platform.
installation: Use the official website to create an account.
example2: Export and review relationships in the investigation results
safety: Check current licensing and data-handling terms.

name: ExifTool
description: Reads and writes metadata in images, documents, audio, and video files.
example2: exiftool -GPS:All -DateTimeOriginal photograph.jpg
safety: Metadata can be missing, altered, or misleading; preserve original evidence.

name: FOCA
description: Analyses document metadata and discovers metadata-related information.
installation: Download the release from the official GitHub repository; Windows/.NET requirements apply.
example1: Open FOCA and create a project for an authorised domain
example2: Analyse a locally obtained PDF or DOCX for metadata
safety: Use documents you own or are permitted to examine.

name: Metagoofil
description: Searches for publicly indexed documents and extracts available metadata.
installation: git clone https://github.com/opsdisk/metagoofil.git && cd metagoofil && pip install -r requirements.txt
example2: python3 metagoofil.py -d example.com -t pdf -l 20 -o results -f report.html
safety: Search-provider support changes; avoid collecting sensitive documents unnecessarily.

name: PhoneInfoga
description: Provides phone-number format and public-source investigation workflows.
example2: docker run --rm sundowndev/phoneinfoga scan -n '+14155552671'
safety: Use your own number or one with explicit permission; results are not identity proof.

name: Holehe
description: Checks whether an email may be registered on supported services via public response behaviour.
example2: holehe --help
safety: Use only your own email or an authorised test address; avoid targeting individuals.

name: Have I Been Pwned
description: Checks whether an email address appears in known breach datasets and supports breach notifications.
installation: No installation required; API access requires an API key.
example1: Visit https://haveibeenpwned.com/ and check your own email
example2: curl -s -H 'hibp-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY' -H 'user-agent: OSINT-Lab' 'https://haveibeenpwned.com/api/v3/breaches'
safety: Never use exposed credentials; follow API terms and protect keys.

name: DeHashed
description: Search platform for breach and exposure intelligence under controlled access.
installation: Web service; account and subscription may be required.
example1: Review the platform's search documentation before querying
example2: Use an authorised organisation-domain exposure workflow
safety: Do not search for or disclose other people's passwords or secrets.

name: IntelX
description: Searches indexed public and historical data sources, including selected leak and archive datasets.
installation: Web service; API access depends on plan.
example2: Search a known public document hash or URL
safety: Do not retrieve, redistribute, or exploit stolen personal data.

name: VirusTotal
description: Aggregates malware and URL/domain/IP analysis from multiple security vendors.
installation: Web service; API access requires a key.
example1: Search a known file hash in VirusTotal
example2: Inspect the report for a domain you own
safety: Do not upload confidential files; submissions may be shared with security partners.

name: AlienVault OTX
description: Community threat-intelligence platform for indicators, pulses, and threat context.
installation: Web service; API access available with account.
example1: Search an IP address in OTX
example2: Review a pulse related to a malware family
safety: Validate indicators with additional sources before blocking.

name: urlscan.io
description: Analyses website loads, contacted domains, resources, screenshots, and technologies.
installation: No local installation; web service and API available.
example2: Submit a non-sensitive URL you own for analysis
safety: Do not submit private URLs, tokens, or internal systems.

name: Wayback Machine
description: Provides historical snapshots of publicly archived websites.
example2: Compare archived snapshots from two dates
safety: Archived content may be incomplete and is not proof of current state.

name: Google Advanced Search
description: Uses search operators and filters to find publicly indexed information.
example2: site:example.com intitle:privacy
safety: Search indexing is incomplete; do not use queries to access restricted content.

name: Bing Search
description: Search engine useful for discovering indexed websites, documents, and public references.
example2: "example.com" -site:example.com
safety: Search results vary by region and time; corroborate findings.

name: Google Lens
description: Visual search tool for finding visually similar images, objects, and public web matches.
installation: Use Google Lens in browser or supported mobile app.
example1: Upload a permitted image to find visually similar public images
example2: Select a visible object in an image to search for related information
safety: Avoid uploading sensitive or private images without consent.

name: TinEye
description: Reverse image search engine used to find matching or modified copies of an image.
example1: Upload an image you own to search for matching copies
example2: Paste a public image URL into the search box
safety: A match does not establish the original photographer or date.

name: Bellingcat Online Investigation Toolkit
description: Curated collection of tools and methods for open-source investigations and verification.
example1: Choose the Geolocation category and follow a listed resource
example2: Choose the Image/Video Verification category for a practical workflow
safety: Use documented verification methods and preserve source context.

name: OpenStreetMap
description: Collaborative map data useful for geographic context and location research.
installation: No installation; web map and open data.
example1: Search for a public landmark by name
example2: Inspect nearby roads and points of interest around a known public location
safety: Respect privacy; avoid exposing private residences or vulnerable people.

name: Google Earth
description: Provides satellite imagery and geographic visualisation for location research.
installation: Install Google Earth or use the web version.
example2: Compare available historical imagery for a public site
safety: Imagery dates and resolution vary by location.

name: Wikimapia
description: Community-mapped geographic descriptions and points of interest.
example1: Search for a public institution by name
example2: Compare community annotations with independent map sources
safety: Community annotations can be inaccurate; verify independently.

name: ADS-B Exchange
description: Provides aircraft tracking data from ADS-B receivers and related services.
example1: Search a publicly visible aircraft registration
example2: Review a historical flight track where access is available
safety: Coverage and historical data depend on receiver network and service tier.

name: MarineTraffic
description: Ship tracking and maritime intelligence based on AIS and related sources.
example1: Search a vessel by IMO or MMSI
example2: Inspect a vessel's public port-call history where available
safety: AIS can be incomplete, delayed, or intentionally absent.

name: OpenCorporates
description: Searches company records aggregated from public corporate registries.
example1: Search a company by registered name
example2: Compare company registration details across jurisdictions
safety: Confirm legal status with the relevant official registry.

name: SEC EDGAR
description: Official database of filings by companies and other entities subject to U.S. SEC reporting.
example1: Search a public company by name or ticker
example2: Open a 10-K filing and review risk factors
safety: This covers U.S. filings; other countries have separate registries.

name: Companies House
description: Official UK company register with filings, officers, and company status information.
example1: Search a UK company by name
example2: Review filing history and company status
safety: Personal data may be limited; follow applicable data protection rules.

name: GitHub Search
description: Searches public repositories, code, users, and project activity.
example1: Search repositories for a project name
example2: Search public code for a non-sensitive configuration keyword
safety: Do not use results to access exposed secrets; report leaks responsibly.

name: Gitleaks
description: Detects potential secrets in repositories and files to help prevent accidental exposure.
installation: Install from the official releases or: go install github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/v8@latest
example2: gitleaks dir /path/to/your-project
safety: Scan only repositories you own or are authorised to assess; treat matches as sensitive.

name: TruffleHog
description: Scans repositories and other supported sources for exposed credentials and secrets.
installation: Install from official releases; see project documentation.
example2: trufflehog github --repo https://github.com/your-org/your-repo
safety: Use only on owned or authorised repositories; never validate discovered credentials by logging in.

name: YARA
description: Pattern-matching tool used to classify and examine files with custom rules.
example2: yara rule.yar sample.bin
safety: Analyse malware only in an isolated lab; rules can produce false positives.

name: Sigma
description: Generic detection-rule format for describing suspicious log events across SIEM platforms.
example2: sigma convert -t splunk rules/windows/
safety: Validate generated queries in a test environment before production deployment.

name: Wireshark
description: Packet analyser for inspecting network traffic and protocol behaviour.
example2: tshark -r capture.pcap -Y 'http.request'
safety: Capture and inspect only traffic you are authorised to access.

name: theZoo
description: Malware sample archive intended for research and education.
installation: Review repository safety guidance before any use.
example1: Read the repository documentation and safety warnings
example2: Use only in a disposable, isolated malware-analysis lab
safety: Malware samples are dangerous; do not download or execute on a normal workstation.

name: OSINT Framework
description: Interactive directory of OSINT resources organised by investigation type.
example1: Open the Email category to discover email research resources
example2: Open the Username category to discover username research resources
safety: A directory is a discovery aid; verify each linked tool's safety and status.

name: OSINT Combine
description: Collection of OSINT resources, training, and investigation utilities.
example1: Explore the resource directory for a specific investigation type
example2: Use a training resource to practise source verification
safety: Check the terms and availability of each linked resource.

name: IntelTechniques Tools
description: Collection of search tools and methods for researching public information.
example1: Choose a search tool for a public business name
example2: Use a public-record search resource for a permitted research task
safety: Follow local privacy and data-protection laws.

name: Google Maps
description: Maps, business listings, imagery, and geographic context for public places.
example2: Use Street View to examine a public-facing location
safety: Do not use geolocation techniques to target or expose private individuals.

name: Have I Been Pwned Domain Search
description: Allows verified domain owners to understand exposure of email addresses associated with their domain.
installation: No installation; domain verification and service access required.
example1: Verify your organisation's domain using the official workflow
example2: Review the authorised domain's breach exposure summary
safety: Only domain owners or authorised administrators should use this workflow.
